course_name_original: Introduction to Finite Elements for Mechanical Systems
course_name_en: Introduction to Finite Elements for Mechanical Systems

learning_outcomes.text: basic concepts of finite elements for bar constructions in static applications
the student can fully compile a matrix formulation, code in Matlab/Python, carry out a complete analysis, and interpret results
demonstrate the modular nature of the method and make connections to other courses in the curriculum where these points are addressed
mathematical modeling of a continuous system with discrete degrees of freedom
coding of a problem in a matrix formulation

syllabus_topics: Context and fundamental concepts of discretization
Composition of system matrices - Based on physical principles (for 2D problems)
Stiffness matrix of a bar element (truss structures)
Stiffness matrix of a beam element
Derived from energy statements in displacement formulation
System equations
Element stiffness matrix
System stiffness matrix
Coordinate transformations (for 3D problems)
Properties of the system matrix
Definition of boundary conditions and loads
Solution of the system of equations
Postprocessing of the results
Basic non-linear analysis (geometric non-linearity)
Outlook on the extension from 1D elements to 2D and 3D elements
Truss structure (with hinged nodes)
Straight beam structure with orthogonal elements
Planar structure with inclined/curved beams in 2D
Bar structure in 3D
Comparison of the previous exercises with an analysis in commercial Finite Element (FE) software.

assessment_methods.method: Partial or continuous assessment with (final) exam

institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
